text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with LLMs through prompts, and prompt engineering means writing clear instructions to get better results. LLMs are good at tasks like summarising, translating and answering questions. However, they have limits: they can make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce false facts. They also cannot truly understand meaning like humans do.
